core_obligations: Conditions (1) and (2) of the weak Serre criterion: zero is quasi-coherent and the subcategory is strictly full (proof lines 3670-3677).

Condition (3): for $\varphi : \mathcal{G} \to \mathcal{F}$ quasi-coherent on the site, transport via $g_!$ (quasi-coherent by the shriek lemma), cokernel quasi-coherent on $\mathcal{X}$ (Sheaves on Stacks lemma), exactness of $g^*$ identifies $\mathrm{Coker}(\varphi)$; the kernel lies in LQCoh^{fbc} by the base-change proposition and maps back to a quasi-coherent module (proof lines 3679-3697).

Condition (4): for an extension with quasi-coherent $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{G}$, reduce to $\mathcal{X} = U$ affine via smooth (resp. flat) locality, present $\mathcal{G}$ by free modules after an \'etale (resp. fppf) covering, lift the surjection to $\mathcal{E}$ using $H^1 = 0$ (assembled from pullback identification, cohomology agreement, and affine vanishing on the big site), and conclude with the presentation of $\mathcal{E}$ whose kernel and cokernel terms are quasi-coherent by (3) (proof lines 3699-3765).
proof_roadmap: Check the two easy weak Serre conditions.
Transport (3) through $g_!$ and exact $g^*$ with the LQCoh^{fbc} kernel result.
Lift presentations through vanishing $H^1$ to assemble (4).
difficulty_reason: The proof verifies all four weak Serre conditions with real work in (3) and (4): kernels are produced through the $g_!$-$g^*$ transport (shriek pushforward quasi-coherent, cokernel quasi-coherent on $\mathcal{X}$, exactness of $g^*$, and the LQCoh^{fbc} membership of kernels via the base-change proposition), and the extension argument lifts a presentation of $\mathcal{G}$ through the vanishing of $H^1$ assembled from three cited results, finishing with a presentation of $\mathcal{E}$.
